newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: New air raid on Kabul.
newsitem.headline: New air raid on Kabul.

text.p: An airplane dropped several bombs on Kabul on Wednesday night in the sixth such air raid in five days.
The night sky was lit up with tracer fire as anti-aircraft gunners of the islamic Taleban, who took the Afghan capital in September, tried to bring the attacking aircraft down.
It was not immediately clear where the bombs fell, but Kabul airport in the northern suburbs which is used for both military and civilian traffic has been frequently targeted in the past.
It was not known if there were any casualties.

There has been a spate of air-raids since Saturday when opposition planes launched four attacks in one day. Six people were injured in Saturday's bombings and one woman was wounded in the head by falling anti-aircraft rounds, according to local hospitals.
The air raids began the day after opposition forces suffered a major defeat at the hands of the Taleban.
Opposition forces were pushed back by 10 km (six miles) on the front line north of Kabul. The Taleban said dozens of opposition fighters were killed and more than 200 were taken prisoner.
Since Saturday there has been little change in the front line, although sporadic exchanges of artillery and rocket fire have continued.

The Taleban, who took Kabul in late September, are facing forces loyal to the ousted government and their ally General Abdul Rashid Dostum some 40 km (25 miles) north of Kabul and in the remote northwestern provinces of Afghanistan.
Attempts by the United Nations to broker a ceasefire between the warring factions have so far been unsuccessful.
